votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 12 of 2024, approving the first amendment to the Interlocal Agreement with the Utah Inland Port Authority (RDA)
votes.description: The RDA Board approved the first amendment to the Interlocal Agreement among Salt Lake City Corporation, the Redevelopment Agency, and the Utah Inland Port Authority, originally executed in October 2022 to comply with March 2022 legislative changes.

votes.motion: Adjourn as the Redevelopment Agency and convene as the Salt Lake City Council
votes.description: Procedural motion to close the RDA board meeting and open the City Council meeting.

votes.motion: Approve the work session meeting minutes of June 4, 2024
votes.description: The Council approved the official minutes from the June 4, 2024 work session meeting.

votes.motion: Adopt Joint Resolution 23 of 2024, recognizing Home Depot and its dedicated employees for their service to Salt Lake City
votes.description: The Council adopted a joint ceremonial resolution with Mayor Mendenhall honoring Home Depot and its employees for their community service contributions to Salt Lake City.

votes.motion: Close the Public Hearing and refer Item E-1 (Summer Snacks for Youth Programs Grant) to a future Consent Agenda for action
votes.description: The Council closed the public hearing on the grant application for the Summer Snacks for Youth Programs and referred it to a future consent agenda for final action.

votes.motion: Close the Public Hearing on Fiscal Year 2024-25 Capital Improvement Program and hold another Public Hearing on August 13, 2024
votes.description: The Council closed the first public hearing on the FY2024-25 CIP budget and scheduled a second public hearing for August 13, 2024 before taking final action.

votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 24 of 2024, endorsing the Capital City Revitalization Zone Project Area and the Participation Agreement between Salt Lake City and Smith Entertainment Group (SEG), with additional legislative intents regarding Japantown funding, construction mitigation, transit prioritization, and comprehensive planning
votes.description: The Council endorsed the Capital City Revitalization Zone Project Area and Participation Agreement with SEG, which outlines use of sales tax revenue to develop the project area, and added directives on Japantown infrastructure funding options, a construction mitigation process, transit development prioritization, and an inclusive planning process for all phases.

votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 20 of 2024, authorizing Addendum Number 8 to the Interlocal Agreement with the Utah Transit Authority
votes.description: The Council authorized the Mayor to enter into Addendum No. 8 to the UTA Interlocal Agreement to implement 2024-25 Frequent Transit Network service on key bus routes with at least 15-minute frequency.

votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 21 of 2024, intending to designate an assessment area for economic promotion activities in downtown over a three-year period (CBIA-25)
votes.description: The Council adopted a resolution of intention to designate the Central Business Improvement Area for a new three-year period from April 2025 to April 2028, continuing the special assessment on downtown commercial properties for economic promotion activities.

votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 25 of 2024, authorizing the issuance or periodic incurrence of short-term revolving obligations (Airport Revolving Line of Credit), and refer to the Consent Agenda to set a hearing date for August 13, 2024
votes.description: The Council approved a revolving line of credit of up to $400 million to fund ongoing Airport Redevelopment Project work at lower interest rates until the next bond issuance, and scheduled a public hearing for August 13, 2024.

votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 22 of 2024, approving the first amendment to the Interlocal Agreement with the Utah Inland Port Authority (City Council)
votes.description: The City Council approved the same first amendment to the Interlocal Agreement with the Utah Inland Port Authority that the RDA Board had approved earlier in the meeting, authorizing the Mayor to execute it in her capacity as Mayor of Salt Lake City Corporation.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 58 of 2024, approving a $100,000 loan for Goat Head, LLC, from the Economic Development Loan Fund
votes.description: The Council approved a $100,000 EDLF loan to Goat Head, LLC, a vegan/vegetarian restaurant at 702 South 300 East, to support creation of four new jobs and retention of two existing jobs. Council Member Mano recused himself.
The Council approved all consent agenda items, including setting public hearing dates for multiple ordinances and resolutions, and approving board appointments and reappointments.
